notes.title: The hunt under water
items: The dive is busier: dozens of new animals at Catalina and in the islands, from barred sand bass, bonito and barracuda to a curious giant sea bass, a mola and a blue shark out in the blue. Scallops, urchins and conch can be taken by hand; abalone are only to look at.
Press 2 to watch yourself swim from behind, in mask and long fins with the gun out ahead. 1 goes back to the mask.
Press Q to lock on to a fish, lobster or shellfish while you close in. It shows the kind, size, range and whether it is legal. It never fires for you. Q again moves to the next, Shift+Q lets go.

Shooting is a hunt now. Lead a passing yellowtail, get right over a halibut, take a stone shot just behind the eye, or work a body-shot fish up the line between its surges before it wraps the kelp. The bead on the muzzle is green only when a shot would hit.
Each dive names a fish or two to look for, worth extra. Leave your catch on the float too long near sea lions and one will help itself.
The water moves and looks better: swaying kelp, a rolling surface overhead, softer light, silt off the sand, schools that turn together and open round you.
Sizes, limits and habits of the new animals are from memory, not from the current regulations.

notes.title: The real Catalina
items: Santa Catalina and the Long Beach shore are now drawn from satellite pictures and real elevation: the island has its true shape and height, with Mount Orizaba, the dip at the Isthmus and Avalon's bay, and the land wears its real colours.
Coastlines on every water are smooth now instead of stair-stepped.

Avalon and Two Harbors are rebuilt on the real waterfront. The Casino stands on its point, the green pier runs out into the middle of the bay, and the pier, the mole and the Two Harbors pier are solid to boats.
Some marks moved with the coast: the Shoreline start, the Avalon fuel dock, Emerald Bay and the no-take circles at the dive park, Lover's Cove and Blue Cavern.
Far from shore the picture no longer shakes: off Long Beach, at Avalon and out at the Farallones the sea, the shadows on deck and the wakes are as steady as on the Bay.

notes.title: Long Beach, the oil rigs and Avalon
items: Long Beach to Catalina is now a place to go. The breakwater is a wall of rock with two lit gates, the four oil islands stand off the beach with their palms and painted towers, and the Queen Mary lies under downtown.

Out in the channel the oil platforms Edith, Ellen, Elly and Eureka are solid steel, lit like small towns at night, with the Catalina boats, ships in the lanes and the morning's sportfishers running past. Fish their up-current side from outside the 100 metre ring.

Avalon has its round white Casino, the green pier, a harbour full of moorings and a waterfront to walk: land at the dinghy dock or the fuel dock and press O. Two Harbors has its pier, its bar and the road across the Isthmus.
Fuel and repairs at Avalon and the Isthmus, kelp along the island's lee shore, and three new races.

notes.title: A richer sea under the surface
items: Under water is a place worth going now: a kelp forest at Catalina with blades streaming in the surge and light shafts through the canopy, ledges, holes and sand channels on the bottom, and coral heads, sea fans and sponges in the BVI.

Fish look like themselves and school together, parting round you: clouds of blacksmith and sardines, calico bass under the canopy, sheephead, a garibaldi coming to look, a bat ray on the sand, a seal circling.
There is a real speargun in your hand, with a shaft that leaves on its line, and the panel is a dive computer. The sailing instruments stay out of the way until you climb out.
Lobsters caught in the practice setting earn a small practice award and are not counted in your logbook.

notes.title: Fishing off Long Beach and Catalina
items: Off Long Beach and Catalina the fishing is now Southern California's own: calico in the kelp, halibut on the harbor sand, rockfish under the oil platforms, and yellowtail, dorado and the odd tuna out in the channel.

Tow a lure while you cruise, drift a live sardine from the bait barge at Alamitos Bay, or stop short of the birds and cast. Fight what takes it by holding L while it rests and letting go while it runs.
Every fish scores by its size for its kind, with a running total for the day and your personal bests on the Logbook tab.
Shift+L opens the fishing card: what is biting and why, and tournaments you can call against the club's skippers or your friends.

notes.title: A 22 ft centre console
items: A 22 ft centre console joins the boats: no sails, one big outboard, 26 knots at cruise and 40 flat out. I starts her; full stop and comma work the throttle, and holding them runs the lever up or down.
The sea sets her speed. Drive her into a chop faster than it allows and she leaves the water, lands hard and starts to break. The readout tells you what the sea will stand.
She crosses from Long Beach to Avalon in under an hour on a sixth of her tank, draws less than half a metre, and is the suggested boat on the Catalina water.
She does not race against the sailing boats, and carries the kayak on her T-top.

notes.title: Go ashore on foot
items: You can now go ashore on foot: step off at a dock, land the tender at a bar, or press O with the boat lying off a guest dock, and you are standing on the float. W A S D walk, Shift jogs, Q, E or a drag look round.

Press F to sit at a table, take a bar stool, lean on the rail or dance. G at the bar opens the menu (a Painkiller in the BVI, on the house for now), and 1 to 5 wave, say cheers, point, shrug or laugh.

Friends ashore at the same place appear as themselves, with their name, their drink and what they type in a bubble over their head. Anyone can stand the whole deck a round, and T tells every boat on the water where you are.
O back at the dock takes you aboard.

notes.title: Over the side: freediving, a speargun and lobster
items: Press 5 at anchor or on a mooring to go over the side with mask, fins and a speargun. The arrow keys are your fins: kick, glide, and watch your lungs. Resting on the float before a dive gives you longer under.
Stalk slowly and shoot inside four metres (F). Read each fish's rule first: a protected fish or a short one is a citation, and reserves keep the gun on safe.
Lobster are taken by hand (G), from the front, measured and bagged only in season. Key 6 is a practice setting for an October night.

Clean dives grow your freediving level in the logbook, from 45 seconds and 8 metres toward two and a half minutes and 25. This is a first cut: dive sites are in the British Virgin Islands and at Catalina, and the underwater scenery will get richer.

notes.title: A new water: Long Beach to Catalina
items: A new water: the San Pedro Channel, from Long Beach across 22 miles of open water to Avalon or the Isthmus on Santa Catalina Island.
It replays 19 and 20 July 2025: a calm dawn, a light southerly morning and a 10 to 13 knot westerly every afternoon, with a long low south swell.
Start from Shoreline Marina or Alamitos Bay, pick up a mooring at Avalon or Isthmus Cove, or anchor in Catalina Harbor. The crossing is there to race.
Coming to this water: a centre console powerboat, local fishing, diving for lobster, the oil islands and the town at Avalon.

notes.title: A dinghy and a wave runner
items: Your tender is now your choice. Every yacht carries the kayak, every boat a dinghy with an outboard that planes at 15 knots, and the catamaran, the 45 and the 50 a wave runner that does 38.
Anchor or pick up a mooring, then press O to launch. Shift+O changes tender while it is stowed. Hold Shift with W to go flat out.
The dinghy skids in tight turns and can swamp driven flat out into a blow. Throw the wave runner round at full speed and you fall off; she circles back for you.
Mind the harbour's five knots, land at any bar's guest dock, and your friends now see you zip past.

notes.title: Setting up a race is easier
items: The race panel (R) scrolls again: on smaller screens its lower half was cut off, so the courses below the first few and the button to start could not be reached.
Setting up a race is three steps: the course (each shows its length and number of marks), when, and the boats. One button at the bottom is always in view and says exactly what it will do.
For a race later, pick a time in one tap: in 30 minutes, in an hour, tonight at 7:30, or tomorrow evening. Or choose Today or Tomorrow and type a time. Times are shown on your own clock.

notes.title: The water, the sails and the light
items: The water now tells you what the wind is doing: gusts show as dark patches where the wind really is stronger, whitecaps build from about ten knots, and every boat, ferry and ship leaves a wake that curls behind her. Spray flies when she slams into a sea.

The sails take their shape from how you trim them, and shiver and flog when you pinch or let them go. Choose your own sailcloth and spinnaker design on the new Sails page of the Profile tab (B); everyone on the water sees them.
The day runs on through a golden evening into a starlit night with the moon in its real phase, and every boat shows her red, green and white lights, so you can tell which way she is heading.
Summer fog pours through the Golden Gate in the afternoon, and on the Extreme level rain squalls come down the wind at you. A Graphics setting on the way in (Auto, High, Low) helps slower machines.

notes.title: A new water: the British Virgin Islands
items: A new water: the British Virgin Islands, from Jost Van Dyke to Virgin Gorda's North Sound, sailed in the real trade winds and tides of 9 February 2025.
Clear water shows turquoise over the shoals, palms line the beaches, and boats lie on the moorings at the Bight, Cooper Island and North Sound.
Twenty famous stops to go ashore at, from the Willy T and the Baths to Foxy's, the Soggy Dollar and Bitter End.
Race the channel sprint, round Norman and Peter, or go bar to bar from Soper's Hole to Bitter End. Pick the Christmas winds start for a proper blow.

notes.title: A new water: the Gulf of the Farallones
items: A new water: the open Pacific outside the Golden Gate, from the bridge out to the Farallon Islands, north to Point Reyes and Bodega Bay and south to Pillar Point.
Twenty tankers, container ships, car carriers and cruise ships run the real shipping lanes in and out of the Gate every day, with the pilot boat at the sea buoy and fishing boats offshore.
The Potato Patch, the bar and the island refuge are marked on the chart, the crew warns you as you sail into them, and the lighthouses flash at night.

Race to the Lightship, round the Farallones, or up the coast to Drakes Bay and Bodega, on a real July day with a north-wester and a metre of Pacific swell. This water replays 26 July 2024, a breezier day than the Bay's.

notes.title: Company on the water
items: More boats now live on both waters: cruising yachts, daysailers, fishing boats, kayakers and boats at anchor, and every player sees them in the same places.

Hail one with Enter when she is close and she answers with where she is bound, then a tip about the wind, the tide, a place to anchor or the fishing. Sail alongside one and she may race you to the next point. Every boat you meet is counted in your logbook.

The Bay has tankers to the refineries, a second container ship, a car carrier, a cruise ship at Pier 27, tugs with barges and the pilot boat. The San Juans have their car ferry. Ships hold their course and sound five short blasts.
The radio gives each caller a voice of their own, ducks the wind and water while someone speaks, and reads the weather every other hour.

notes.title: Bars and yacht clubs on the shore
items: Every bar and yacht club now has a home on the shore you can steer for: a clubhouse under its burgee, a deck of umbrellas, a guest dock, and lights that come on at dusk.
Sam's in Tiburon has its big deck of white umbrellas. The Corinthian, St. Francis, Richmond and Orcas Island yacht clubs are on the water too, with more places in the San Juans.
As you close with a place its name and distance appear, with a tick once you have been ashore. The chart marks clubs with a flag and bars with a glass.
The boats in the marinas are proper yachts now, and the trees along the waterfront are the right size.

notes.title: Two levels of autopilot
items: P now has two levels. Press once and the pilot steers while you trim the sails. Press again and the crew trims too, so she sails herself. A third press hands everything back.
Steering alone is unlimited, in a race or out, but your speed still depends on your own trimming.
In a race the full pilot is limited to 3 minutes from the gun. The race line shows what is left, and when it runs out the pilot keeps steering and the sheets come back to you.
Before the gun both levels are unlimited, so getting to the start stays easy. The spinnaker is yours to trim unless the full pilot is on.

notes.title: A real sea
items: The Bay now has a real sea. The chop builds with the wind and the open water to windward, stands up short and steep where the ebb runs against the breeze in the Golden Gate, and lies down in the lee of the land.

Your boat lives in it: she loses speed punching into a chop (the 30 far more than the 45), slams when she falls off a steep one, surfs a little running in a big sea, and is harder to steer and easier to gybe by accident downwind.

Ships and ferries leave a wake that reaches you a minute or so after they pass, rolling the boat and shaking the wind out of the sails in light air. In the kayak, turn your bow into a big ship's wake or it will put you over.
The instruments describe the sea beside the wind, and there are new tips for chop, slamming and wind against tide.

notes.title: Tips, and a radio you can see
items: Small cards now pop up at the right moment to show a key you may not know: hold V to talk when another boat appears, J to reef when it blows, X near an anchorage, O to go ashore. Each goes away once you use the key, and Don't show tips turns them off.
The radio has a light at the bottom left. It shows RX when anyone is on the air and TX when you are. Click it to learn how the radio works.
The Keys tab on the board is grouped, searchable, and marks keys that are new since you last sailed.
The strip of keys at the start of a sail now changes with what you are doing: sailing, racing, at anchor or in the kayak.

notes.title: A catamaran and a bluewater 50
items: Two new boats: a 42 ft cruising catamaran and a 50 ft bluewater cruiser.

The catamaran sails flat and fast on a reach, beating the 45 from about 16 knots, but will not point and is slow through a tack. She gives no heel to warn you: reef by the numbers on her placard, 18 knots apparent and again at 25, or risk a capsize she will not come back from.
Her two engines spin her on the spot, and she floats where the keelboats run aground.
The bluewater 50 is heavy and steady: slow to get going, hard to stop, and at her best when the wind gets up.

notes.title: The beer can league
items: The pace boats are now the yacht club: sixteen skippers, from two ringers who never miss a shift to the couple out for the sunset.

Call a race with up to nine of them and pick the fleet: Beer can, Mixed or Hot. They sail the same boat as you. The weaker ones lose the way real crews do: late starts, sheets left cleated, wide roundings, a reef too late in a blow.
The race panel shows the whole fleet as cards: each boat in her colour with her skipper, and a real player's own figure. Places and gaps show while racing.
At the finish there is a results table that fills in as the back-markers come home. The skippers call across the water in character.

notes.title: Choose your weather
items: On the way in, under the time of day, choose how hard it blows: Lighter, As it was, or Extreme.
Lighter is about two thirds of the recorded wind: gentle and forgiving for a first sail.
Extreme is half as much again, 20 knots and more with hard gusts. She can be knocked flat or gybe by accident. Reef early with J.
Boats sailing together share one wind: the strongest anyone chose.

notes.title: Wind shadow and collisions
items: Boats now take each other's wind. Sail close to leeward of another boat and you lose up to a third of your breeze. The instruments show it and a line tells you whose shadow you are in. Pace boats feel yours too.
Boats no longer pass through each other. A collision stops you against the other hull and costs hull damage that grows with the closing speed: a scuff at one knot, a third of the hull at four.
A damaged hull is slower, up to 30 percent. Lie alongside a dock to repair her, or she mends slowly at anchor outside a race.
Hit hard enough and she is holed: you are out of the race and put back afloat nearby a few seconds later. Ferries and ships hit harder.

notes.title: A start you can aim at
items: Every race mark now has a ring on the water at its true distance, 130 metres. Sail into the ring and the mark is yours, with a chime and a line giving the bearing and distance to the next one.
Before the gun, the line under the clock shows how far the start ring is and whether you would reach it early or late at your present speed. The crew call it at five, two and one minutes.
Inside the start ring when the gun goes, you have started. Otherwise sail into it.
A boat towed to the start is now left sailing toward the start mark, not head to wind. G hides the rings and the coaching.

notes.title: The radio: channel 16
items: Ferries and ships now call on the radio as they leave a berth or come through the Golden Gate, and call you by name if they are about to pass close. Shift+V turns the calls off.
On the website, hold V to talk to every boat on your water, with the sound of a real VHF set. Release to listen. A light among the hails shows who is transmitting.
Your browser asks for the microphone the first time you press V. Refuse and you can still listen.
Voice is on the website only for now, and reaches up to eight boats on a water.

notes.title: Home screen, your own skipper, and the engine
items: A home screen: returning skippers cast off in one press with the boat and water they used last.
Build your skipper on the new Profile tab (B): ten outfits from foul-weather gear to a lobster suit, hats, hair, face and build, or Surprise me. Other players see your skipper at the helm.
On the website a circle in the corner shows who is signed in, and opens your profile. Signing in has moved from the Logbook tab to the Profile tab.
Every boat has an inboard diesel. I starts and stops it. Full stop steps the throttle up and comma steps it down, through neutral into astern.
A row under the instruments shows revs, fuel and battery while the engine runs. A dock refuels her. No engine in a race.

notes.title: Experience points and ranks
items: Sail her well and you earn points: a clean tack or gybe, time in the groove with both sails trimmed and the boat near her best speed, a gust handled. Doing it with the wheel and sheets in your own hands earns several times what the autopilot does.
Racing pays most: points for each mark and for finishing, and a large award for a win, bigger for every boat you beat. People count for more than pace boats.
Small awards for anchoring cleanly, a night aboard, a first landing, a fish or crab, and a first sighting of an animal. Small penalties for a knockdown, a crash gybe or running aground.
Nine ranks from Deckhand to Admiral. Your rank, points and what earned them are on the Logbook tab. Y hides the award lines.
Nothing can be bought with points yet. That comes later.

notes.title: One boat for the race, a spinnaker, and wind that bites
items: One-design racing. Whoever calls or fixes a race chooses the class, and everyone who joins sails that boat for the race, in their own name and colours. Pace boats too. You get your own boat back afterwards.

A spinnaker. N hoists and douses it once the wind is aft of the beam; Q and E work its sheet. It is worth up to a sixth more speed on a broad reach. Carry it too close to the wind or in too much breeze and she broaches. It has to come down before a tack.
Hard wind knocks her down. On the blowy afternoon, full sail with the sheets pinned in 24 knots and more lays her flat. Ease the main with S as the gust hits, or reef.
Reefing. J puts a reef in the mainsail, Shift and J shakes it out. One reef makes 20 to 25 knots sailable.
Pace boats set spinnakers downwind and reef when it blows.

notes.title: A blowy afternoon
items: A fourth time to cast off on San Francisco Bay: a blowy afternoon, with 20 to 22 knots across the Bay and gusts to 26. Everyone on the water shares the same wind, so if one boat brings the blow, all have it.

notes.title: Fix a race for later and send the link
items: In the race panel (R), choose a course, type the time for the gun, and press Fix the race. On bajaregatta.com you get a link to send: whoever opens it gets your race on the way in.
Boats already on the water with you are told too. The race opens for joining 25 minutes before the gun, and joining tows everyone to the start.

notes.title: The city, as it looks from the water
items: San Francisco's skyline is now the real one: Salesforce Tower, the Transamerica Pyramid, Coit Tower on its hill, the Ferry Building, Sutro Tower behind, and Oracle Park beside McCovey Cove.
Alcatraz has its cellhouse, lighthouse and water tower. The Bay Bridge has its four towers, double deck and centre anchorage, with the white east span beyond.
The waterfront has its pier sheds, Pier 39, Ghirardelli and the square-rigger Balclutha.
At dusk the windows and the bridge lights come on.

notes.title: Race marks you can see, and a living Bay
items: Race marks. Every mark still to round is a big orange buoy. The next one has a column of light over it and its name and range beside it, and a line of arrowheads on the water runs from your bow to it. G turns the guide on and off, and it works for a plain route too.
The race panel no longer jumps back to the top or misses clicks while you choose a course and pace boats.

Wildlife. Harbor porpoise in the Gate and Raccoon Strait, sea lions on the floats at Pier 39, harbor seals in the quiet coves, pelicans, cormorants and gulls, and now and then a humpback on the flood. The crew calls each one out the first time, with a bearing. A card in your logbook keeps count.

Fishing by the tide. Halibut bite on moving water and stop at slack, stripers like the turn of the tide, and trolling under diving birds is better. Lure speeds are the real ones: 6 knots catches nothing. Dungeness inside the Bay all go back; rock crab are the keepers.
The kayak paddles like one: 3 knots at a cruise, Shift with W to sprint until you are blown, a head wind that slows you and a beam wind that turns you.

notes.title: Everyone starts together, and a second place to sail
items: Join a race from anywhere and you are towed to the start area, a few hundred metres short of the first mark, in your own berth beside the others. The same goes for whoever calls it.

San Juan Islands, first cut. Choose the water on the way in: Friday Harbor, Roche Harbor, Sucia and the passes between, with NOAA's wind and the Salish Sea's tides from 25 June 2025. The tide runs 3 to 5 knots there, so start in the late morning near slack water. The land is plain green hills for now and there are no ferries yet.
Boats on different waters do not see each other. Tonight's race is on San Francisco Bay.
On the website, bajaregatta.com, other boats, hails and races now work without a Claude account.

notes.title: The bar hop, and the keys in front of you
items: Tied up at a dock (Sam's in Tiburon, Pier 39), O now steps straight ashore. No kayak needed. O again comes back aboard.
A bar-hop card in your logbook (B, then Logbook) lists every place there is to go ashore and stamps each one the first time you land there.
When you finish a race, the standings open by themselves.
The main keys now sit across the top of the screen for the first minute of each sail. Press / to bring them back or put them away.
Tonight's race course now keeps to the middle of Raccoon Strait and gives Angel Island's north-east point a wide berth. Before, a boat on the autopilot could be put ashore there.

notes.title: Race night, and keys you can read
items: Race night: Raccoon Strait to McCovey Cove, gun at 7:30 PM Pacific on Saturday 14 November. Start from Raccoon Strait. The race opens for joining 25 minutes before the gun: press R, then Join, and be at Point Stuart when it goes.
A race can now be fixed for a real time. It shows on the way in and under the clock, and runs without anyone having to call it.
The Keys page is rewritten in plain words, starting with the five keys you need first.

notes.title: The tender is a kayak, and race nights hold their clock
items: The boat you take ashore is now a kayak with a double-bladed paddle, in place of the outrigger canoe. Everything else is the same: anchor or moor, O launches her, W A S D paddle, O lands you at the bars and beaches, O alongside comes back aboard.
Joining friends who are already out, you now take up their time of day, whatever you chose on the way in. A race that has been called keeps its countdown when someone new arrives.
The gun can be set 3 to 20 minutes ahead, so there is time for everyone to get to the start.

notes.title: Ashore by kayak, and a tow off the mud
items: The kayak. With the boat at anchor or on a mooring, O launches the kayak alongside. Paddle with W A S D. The tide carries her, so think before crossing a strong stream.

Go ashore. Run her up on any beach, or come in at Sam's in Tiburon, Ayala Cove, Sausalito, Aquatic Park, Pier 39, Clipper Cove, Horseshoe Cove or McCovey Cove, ease up and press O. Each place you land at goes in your logbook.
O again shoves off. Back alongside the boat, O brings you aboard.
Aground and stuck? U calls for a tow to the nearest deep water.
Fixed: pointing at the wheel, boom and winches with the mouse could stop working after you switched to another window in the middle of a drag. It now recovers by itself.

notes.title: Anchor, spend the night, and catch your supper
items: X stops the boat. Slow down first: under 2 kt she lets go her anchor in up to 25 m of water. Near a mooring or a dock (Ayala Cove, Sam's, Sausalito, Pier 39, Horseshoe Cove) and under 2.5 kt, X picks up the buoy or brings her alongside.
While she is held the sails are stowed, the cover is on the boom, and you can see her rode or mooring line. She swings to the wind and the tide.
X again gets her under way, on the tack with more water ahead.

Z turns in for the night when you are alone on the water. You wake at 06:30 to the next morning's wind and tide, and the night goes in your logbook. She will not let you sleep in a gale or where she would touch bottom at low water.
Other boats see what you are doing: at anchor, on a mooring, alongside.

Crab pots. K drops a pot (up to three, in 4 to 35 m, going slowly). It marks itself with a buoy in your colours. Leave it to soak for three quarters of an hour, come back alongside, and K hauls it. Red rock crab are the keepers inside the Bay; the Dungeness there are mostly too small and go back.

Fishing. L puts a line out. Troll under sail for striped bass, and king salmon out by the Gate. Stop or anchor on the flats for halibut, leopard shark and bat ray, or off the city piers for jacksmelt and perch. When a fish is on you have twelve seconds to strike with L. Undersized fish go back.
Crab and fish landed are counted in your logbook.

notes.title: Racing, and a wind tunnel for your sails
items: Racing. Press R, pick a course and the minutes to the gun, and call it. Everyone on the water is told and can join. Raccoon Strait to McCovey Cove, Round Alcatraz, the Golden Gate dash, or the route on your own chart.
Pace boats. Up to three boats sailed by the autopilot race with you, in the same boat as yours, each a little off the pace. Race them alone or alongside your friends.
A countdown under the clock, the course on your chart, live places while you race, and your time at the finish. Races and wins go in your logbook.
Who is out. The same panel lists every boat on the water with you: skipper, boat, what she is doing, and her range and bearing.
Wind tunnel, suggested by Scott. Press F to see the air over your sails: smooth where it follows the sail, red and broken where a sail is sheeted too hard, grey and shaking where it luffs.
The wind tunnel card also tells you the wind angle your sails, as set, are asking for: steer to the sails, or trim to the course.
Keys. The board (B) now has a page listing every control.
The roadmap is now a board: sprint columns across, lanes for sailing experience, multiplayer, places, platform and progression. Filter by lane, and the most wanted cards rise to the top.

notes.title: Gust warnings and release notes
items: Gust warnings. The readout shows a gust on its way and how long until it reaches you, and says when you are in one. A strong one raises an alert and drops time back to real speed so you can ease the main.
What's new. This page. A marker on the Roadmap link tells you when there is something you have not read.
The recorded weather runs for 36 hours. When a boat reaches the end, the same day now starts over instead of freezing in the dark.
A boat left running for days no longer drags everyone who joins into her clock.

notes.title: Roadmap, feedback and coaching
items: Roadmap. Press B to see what is planned, in releases, and vote things up or down.
Feedback. Tell us what you think or report a problem without leaving the boat. It can attach what the boat was doing at the time.
Point of sail. The readout now names it: close-hauled, beam reach, running, in irons, and which tack you are on.
Coaching hints. If a sail has been luffing or stalled for a while, or you are stuck in irons, one line says what to do. C turns them off.
Hail other boats with Enter. Their words show on your screen.
Places to meet on the chart: McCovey Cove, Ayala Cove, Sam's in Tiburon and more. Click one to add it to your route.
A logbook of your miles, hours and marks, and the fleet's.
Fixed: a boat could come back broken after the game updated under her, and then would not start again.

notes.title: Real 3 km wind, a choice of when to cast off, knockdowns
items: The wind is now NOAA's 3 km HRRR model for 14 July 2024. It builds through the day, funnels through the Gate and shifts the way it did.
Gusts and lulls sized from the model's own gust speeds.
Choose when to cast off: a light morning, the afternoon sea breeze, or the evening as it eases.
Crash gybes. Let the boom fly across in a breeze with the main out and she can be knocked flat.

notes.title: Regatta
items: A new name, and a join screen: where to sail, an optional first lesson, then your boat.
Three boats: a 30 ft sloop, a 38 and a 45 ft performance cruiser. Name her and choose her colours.

notes.title: Autopilot, traffic and sailing in company
items: An autopilot that holds a heading, a wind angle or your route, with the crew trimming.
